scope: Independent native candidate-first fact check and exact final private draft/source review; no publication acceptance.

items.answer_integrity: Grieg is the composer of the original stage music for Ibsen's Peer Gynt; Ibsen is the dramatist. Sibelius and Nielsen are not supported for this specific original score, and Ibsen is a role distractor, not another defensible composer answer.
checked_claims: LA Phil explicitly identifies Ibsen's January 1874 invitation to Grieg and places Morning Mood, opening Suite I, in Act IV set in Africa.
Faber identifies original incidental music Op. 23 and later suites Op. 46 and Op. 55; its retail item is a string-orchestra arrangement and is not treated as the original score.

British Library's manuscript catalogue documents Suite II's four-number form, five-number first printing, and later withdrawal of the Mountain King's Daughter dance. The final article therefore avoids an unqualified movement count and tells readers to check the edition.
items.pedagogy: Separates play text, stage score, concert selection, scene context, and personal listening impression. Listening is conditional; no measured learning outcome is promised.
items.revision_history: Initial unqualified eight-movement/two-four-movement sentence was challenged against the British Library record and removed before this exact final review.

items.answer_integrity: BnF, LA Phil, and Boston Symphony identify Dukas as the composer. Goethe wrote the literary ballad; Ravel, Debussy, and Satie are not defensible composer answers for this named work.
checked_claims: BnF dates the work to 1897 while specifying a composition period of 1896/1897 and calls it a symphonic scherzo after Goethe's Der Zauberlehrling; the final article keeps these date fields distinct.
LA Phil describes a tone poem, broom represented by bassoon, water-carrying and divided-broom episode, master's return, and later Fantasia association.

Boston Symphony supports Goethe's story sequence and says the quiet opening music returns to complete the frame. The final listening cues remain attributed and do not universalize the bassoon association.
items.pedagogy: Separates composer, literary source, later film, source-described orchestration, and optional personal listening observations.
items.revision_history: The initial unqualified composition-in-1897 wording was narrowed to work date 1897 plus composition period 1896–1897 before this exact final review.

limitations: The informative brief and possible prior exposure mean the blind record is candidate-first, not clean first exposure.
